q1_what_did_you_play: Rapid Fire first, spending the 3-Spark bank on it so it costs 0: four hits of 4 into the only enemy on the board, 16 damage. With the bank gone, Kaboom! reverts to its printed cost of 1 and I paid that for another 7, putting Nibbit at 40 - 23 = 17. That left exactly 1 energy for Duck and Cover, 5 Block against the telegraphed 12, so I eat 7 instead of 12 and end at 35/62. The whole shape of the turn is the single question of which attack the Spark discount is spent on, and Rapid Fire prints 2 and deals 16 while Kaboom! prints 1 and deals 7 — the discount is worth more energy and more damage on Rapid Fire, and there is no targeting risk in 'random enemies' because there is only one enemy. Spending it there and paying cash for the cheap attack is the only way to fit both attacks and the Block into 2 energy.
q2_other_line_considered: Rummage. It costs 1 and draws 3, which is the only card in hand that could change what the turn is, so I priced it: it also spends the 3 Sparks, so after it my remaining 1 energy buys Kaboom! at printed cost for 7 damage and no Block, or Duck and Cover for 5 Block and no damage, and Rapid Fire at printed 2 is unaffordable in either case. That trades 16 guaranteed damage plus the Block for three unknown cards I mostly cannot pay for. I also checked the mirror line — Spark on Kaboom!, then Rapid Fire at printed 2 — which costs all my energy for 23 damage and no Block, strictly worse than the same 23 with 5 Block. Both were dismissed quickly; the Rummage line was the one that took actual arithmetic.
q3_what_it_gave_up: The three cards from Rummage, and with them any chance that this hand was hiding a better turn. It also empties the Spark bank now rather than carrying it, so next turn's attacks pay printed cost from zero. And 5 Block is a small answer to a 12 — I still take 7, so the line accepts chip damage rather than trying to blank the hit, which was never available anyway.
q4_different_intent: Not in any way that changes the cards. The attacks are correct against any intent — 23 damage into a 40 HP enemy is the most this hand can produce and the Spark allocation does not depend on what Nibbit does. Duck and Cover is the only thing 1 energy can buy once both attacks are down: if Nibbit had telegraphed a buff or a defensive move instead of the 12, the Block would be wasted, but Rummage is dead by then with the Sparks spent, so I would play it regardless rather than pass. A much larger telegraphed hit would not have helped either, since 5 is all the Block on offer.
